faq: Will Android users keep their accounts from iOS?
If your backend holds accounts, yes: the Android app signs in to the same accounts. If accounts exist only inside the iOS app, we plan the data move first, which Standard and Premium cover.
Do iOS subscribers keep access on Android?
A subscription bought on Apple cannot be moved to Google Play. We can honor access by account login where your policy and Google Play rules allow it, and we check those rules before building.
Can you convert Java code to Kotlin automatically?
Tools convert the syntax, but the result needs cleanup to be good Kotlin. We convert in steps, run tests after each step and fix what the converter gets wrong, so the app keeps working.
What do you need to begin?
A working build or the source of the current product, API notes, brand files and your list of must-keep features. Google Play access is only needed at release time, and we never ask for passwords.
desc:
Ecom Swift LLC handles Android app migration from iOS, web or Java: we rebuild your product as a native Kotlin app, or modernize an older Java one, with accounts and data carried over and tested before anything goes live.

## What is Android app migration?

Android app migration is moving an existing product onto Android, or moving an old Android app onto a modern foundation. It covers three common cases: an iPhone app that needs an Android version, a website or web app that needs a native counterpart, and a Java app that should move to Kotlin and Jetpack Compose.

It is different from a new build because something already exists. The users, the data, the rules and the brand must all survive the move.

## Why migration needs a plan

A direct copy rarely works. Android has its own navigation, back gesture, notifications, permissions and design language. An iOS screen pasted onto Android feels foreign, and users notice. A web app turned into a thin wrapper often feels slow and out of place.

The riskier part is data. Users expect to sign in and find their history, settings and purchases waiting. If accounts do not match, or a subscriber loses access, support requests pile up and trust drops. A written list of what must carry over, made before coding, prevents most of these problems.

## How migration affects reach and maintenance

Android serves a very large audience across many countries and price levels. Offering your product there can reach people your current platform does not. A modern Kotlin codebase also makes future work cheaper: new developers can join sooner, libraries stay current and old Java quirks stop slowing the team.

We cannot promise how many Android users you will gain, since marketing, pricing and your market all matter. What we do promise is a native app that behaves the way Android users expect and keeps your existing users whole.

## What a strong migration includes

- A plan listing every feature, screen, data field and account rule to carry over.
- Screens built the Android way, with Material design and the system back gesture.
- Your existing API connected, so there is one backend for all platforms.
- Account login that matches your current users.
- Data models mapped between old and new, and tested end to end in the larger package.
- Push notifications ported to Firebase Cloud Messaging.
- Play Billing rebuilt when you sell subscriptions or purchases.
- Testing on several Android versions and phone sizes.
- An internal testing release, so you try everything before launch.
- Play listing, screenshots and release support in the fullest package.

## How we work

We begin by studying what you have: the live app or site, the API and the data. Then we write the plan and agree it with you. The Basic package delivers the plan and the first core screens connected to your API. Standard builds a working version of the core product with login, existing data, push and testing across versions. Premium completes the app with billing, data migration checks and Play listing support.

For Java conversion, we move code to Kotlin in stages and test as we go, instead of running a blind automatic conversion.

## What to do and what to skip

**Do:**
- Decide which features are essential for the first Android release.
- Give us access to your API documentation and a test account.
- Explain how iOS and web subscriptions are managed today.
- Plan how users on both platforms will reach the same account.
- Test the update path with real sample data.

**Avoid:**
- Copying iOS layouts without adapting them.
- Moving every feature at once if the first release can be smaller.
- Changing database structures without a backup.
- Assuming a purchase on one store works on another by default.
- Leaving old Java code in place with no plan for its removal.

## Who this is for

A company with a strong iPhone app and customers asking for Android. A website owner who wants a native app with push and offline use. A team with an aging Java app that keeps breaking when libraries update. A startup that built its first version on another platform and now needs an Android product.

## What we need from you

Send the current app or site link, API notes and a short list of must-have features. Access to your backend is given through test accounts, and to code through collaborator invites. We never ask for passwords. If store purchases are involved, we explain what can and cannot carry over before we build.
